page: Microsoft Azure FX48-12ms_v2 is a constrained-core virtual machine instance configured within Azure's compute- and memory-intensive infrastructure. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance exposes 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 260 MB of shared L3 cache and includes advanced instruction support such as AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8. The host configuration pairs these 12 compute threads with an allocation of 1008.0 GB of system memory, yielding an unusually high ratio of 84.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage or discrete GPU accelerators are bundled with the instance, requiring reliance on remote storage solutions.

Benchmark results reflect the high clock frequency and core constraints of the platform. Single-threaded performance reaches the top 10 percent on Geekbench with a score of 2363.0, corroborated by strong results in single-threaded gzip compression at 34.68 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.44 GB/sec. Text processing workloads also register in the top decile. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput falls in the middle 50 percent range, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 11371.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 22916.45, reflecting the low total core count. Memory bandwidth reaches 102.17 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 72.21 GB/sec for writes, with Redis operations achieving 18.91 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the constrained-core design provides distinct economic advantages for software licensed per core, such as relational database engines, while retaining access to massive memory pools and full single-thread clock rates. However, the architecture represents a clear tradeoff: workloads that scale horizontally across high thread counts will find parallel compute throughput limited. The instance is suited for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), analytics engines requiring high memory capacity per core, and memory-bound batch processing.
description: Microsoft Azure FX48-12ms_v2 is a memory-dense, constrained-core virtual machine featuring an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The instance allocates 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores and pairs them with 1008.0 GB of RAM, providing 84.0 GB of memory per core alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates hardware instruction support for AVX-512 and AMX, while omitting local disk storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmarks show top-tier single-core performance, achieving 2363.0 on Geekbench and high throughput in data compression and text parsing tasks, though overall multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the low core count. This architecture provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for environments constrained by per-core software licensing fees, making it particularly suitable for large in-memory relational databases, electronic design automation tooling, and memory-intensive batch analytics.
